record.original_question: Is there a universal countable right-orderable group?

evidence.quote: 2.19∗ . (B. H. Neumann). Is there a universal countable right-orderable group?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A group $G$ is called right-orderable if there exists a total order $\le$ on $G$ such that for all $a,b,c\in G$, $a\le b$ implies $ac\le bc$. A countable right-orderable group $U$ is called universal (for the class of countable right-orderable groups) if every countable right-orderable group embeds into $U$ as a subgroup.

Question: Does there exist a universal countable right-orderable group?
